newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends firm on futures, tight cargoes.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends firm on futures, tight cargoes.

text.p: NWE gasoline strengthened on Tuesday as crude and unleaded gasoline futures reversed recent losses and pulled the physical market higher, traders said.
A raft of prompt Eurograde barge deals were done in the $206.50 to $207.75 a tonne fob AR throughout the day.
Talked levels were as high as $209/$210 at the height of the energy futures spurt higher, but eased to $208.50/$209.50 for first half June delivery towards the end of the day.
Traders said cargoes were being talked at fairly "steamy" levels with premium unleaded cif NWE cargoes on offer around the $217.50 level.
"There's a lot of talk but when it comes to actually buying cargoes there's not that much available," said one trader.
Traders also attributed the steep cargo prices to speculation over U.K. stockpiling ahead of possible tax hikes in the Labour government's post-election mini-budget as well as healthy U.S. demand.

Although, while talk concerning the U.K. auto fuel tax hikes remained rife, a number of traders stressed that if Labour holds its budget on June 10, as slated by political pundits, there was very little gasoline players could do.
"People won't have time to sort material out if the budget is held on June 10, if it's later that's a different story," said one trader.

The U.S. arbitrage door swung open and closed throughout the day with the difference between June Eurograde barges in northwest Europe and July NYMEX unleaded futures standing just below $24 a barrel in late trade.
